page: Microsoft Azure E96pds_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine built on the arm64 architecture, utilizing Microsoft ARM Neoverse-N2 processors clocked at 3.4 GHz. The instance is configured with 96 dedicated physical cores and operates without simultaneous multithreading, dedicating one thread per physical core. Hardware cache allocation includes 64 KB of L1 data cache per core, 1.0 MB of L2 cache per core, and a shared 128 MB L3 cache. Memory capacity totals 672.0 GB, providing an allocation ratio of 7.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. The server bundles 5,670 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD storage, and operates without discrete GPU acceleration.

In benchmark assessments, the E96pds_v6 exhibits moderate single-thread compute metrics alongside top-tier multi-core performance. The single-core stress-ng and Geekbench evaluations fall within the middle 50 percent of tested cloud servers. However, the 96 dedicated physical cores yield top-tier results in multi-threaded benchmarks, including multi-core stress-ng, Clang compilation, and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression at 857.84 GB/sec. The memory subsystem records top-tier results, reaching large-block uncached read speeds of 465.42 GB/sec and write speeds of 205.78 GB/sec. This throughput supports high transaction density, achieving over 170 million operations per second in Redis SET tests and high PassMark database operations scores.

From a cost and architectural efficiency standpoint, the ARM Neoverse-N2 platform achieves high compute and memory density without hyperthreading resource contention. Qualitative tradeoffs include the lack of x86-specific instruction sets such as AVX-512 or AMX, and the absence of hardware accelerators. Consequently, large language model inference is viable for smaller and medium parameter sizes on CPU, but throughput trails GPU-equipped options for heavy deep learning tasks.

The hardware configuration is suitable for memory-heavy, I/O-intensive production workloads. Key target applications include distributed in-memory caching platforms such as Redis, large transactional and analytical databases, high-throughput static web serving, high-concurrency compilation clusters, and data-intensive ETL processing.
description: Microsoft Azure E96pds_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine powered by 96 dedicated ARM Neoverse-N2 cores running at 3.4 GHz without simultaneous multithreading. It provides 672 GB of RAM, delivering 7 GB per physical core, alongside a bundled 5,670 GB local NVMe solid-state drive. Benchmark results show standard single-core execution alongside top-tier multi-core scaling, evidenced by high throughput in multi-threaded decompression, software compilation, and physics simulations. The memory subsystem demonstrates top-tier bandwidth, exceeding 465 GB/s in large uncached block reads and 205 GB/s in writes, which directly benefits data-heavy operations. Redis SET benchmarks exceed 170 million operations per second, matching the instance's high PassMark database ratings. While the absence of x86 vector extensions and dedicated hardware accelerators limits specialized AI training, the server delivers high compute density and cost efficiency across distributed in-memory databases, Redis caches, high-concurrency static web serving, and scalable backend enterprise applications.
